name: Skipper
tagline: Largest domestic transmission-tower manufacturer riding India's T&D grid capex cycle, now backed by a record Rs 9,217cr order book and raised FY27 export guidance - genuinely improving fundamentals, but a leveraged, low-moat, working-capital-heavy EPC-type business that keeps this at 'neither' rather than a return-magnitude label.
business_overview: Skipper Ltd (NSE/BSE: SKIPPER) manufactures power transmission and distribution (T&D) structures/towers, telecom towers, and polymer pipes & fittings, with exports to 60+ countries and a domestic T&D capex-cycle tailwind. Seeded via X (untrusted triage, @RupakRoyC, high conviction bullish view). Is India's largest transmission-tower manufacturer, scaling engineering (tower) capacity from 300,000 MTPA (FY25 start) toward a targeted 600,000 MTPA by FY29.

FY26 revenue ~Rs 5,554 Cr, +20.1% YoY; FY24 +65.8% and FY25 +40.9% both independently confirmed (not artifacts) - a genuine, decelerating-off-a-high-base growth curve
Borrowings up from ~Rs 579 Cr (FY24) to ~Rs 931 Cr (FY26); CARE rates Skipper A+/A1+ (stable), calling debt-servicing comfortable, but cost of borrowing is flagged high by screener

fundamentals_narrative: Skipper is a genuine, evidenced beneficiary of India's T&D grid build-out and export demand for transmission structures: a record Rs 9,217cr order book (commercial evidence, not just a claimed tailwind), management raising FY27 export order-inflow guidance from Rs 650cr to Rs 1,500cr and total order-inflow guidance to Rs 7,500cr mid-year (a credibility positive - guidance was raised, not cut), and a genuinely improving ROCE (9% in FY20-22 to 23-24% in FY23-26, confirmed via screener/CARE this pass, not the previously-flagged unreliable ~48% figure). Set against this: debt has risen materially (Rs579cr->Rs931cr, FY24->FY26) with cost of borrowing flagged as high, FCF conversion remains thin as capex absorbs most operating cash flow, and promoter holding fell sharply from 66.50% to 61.48% in a single recent month (Jun->Jul 2026) - concurrent with a sharp FII holding increase (4.11%->10.64%), consistent with a block-deal/OFS rather than open-market distress selling, but worth watching over the next 1-2 quarters. Working-capital reads are genuinely mixed between sources (CARE says the operating cycle improved; screener's debtor-days metric says it worsened) and were not fully reconciled this pass.

verdict_headline: Entity confirmed as Skipper Ltd (NSE/BSE: SKIPPER). A genuine, now commercially-evidenced T&D-capex-cycle beneficiary - record order book, raised guidance, real ROCE improvement - but rising debt, thin FCF conversion, a fresh promoter stake reduction and no true moat keep this at 'neither' (via analyst override) despite a four_box score of 3.0; conviction upgraded to Medium-High as this pass resolved the prior 'unverified figures' doubt into genuinely confirmed strength.
verdict_reasoning: four_box = 3.0 (tailwind yes - named, now order-book-evidenced T&D capex-cycle and export tailwind; tam yes - expanding grid-infrastructure and telecom-tower demand; moat weak - real backward-integration cost position but multiple large competitors (KEC, Kalpataru) are simultaneously adding capacity into the same cycle; valuation weak - 26.7x trailing P/E against a capital-intensive, working-capital-heavy, increasingly leveraged balance sheet is not clearly 'room to pay'). Score >=3.0 permits a 10x/100x label, but analyst_override is kept: this is capital-intensive, low-moat EPC-type economics (rising debt, thin FCF, commodity-competitive tower manufacturing) that don't fit a 10x-in-2-3-years/100x-in-10-years return-magnitude claim even with genuinely improving fundamentals ('Nesco logic').

Conviction raised from Medium to Medium-High: the prior pass's core doubt (ROCE ~47.8% and growth ~65.7% 'looked anomalously high... not independently reconciled') is now resolved - the real ROCE trajectory (9%->24%) and the FY24 growth figure (confirmed genuine, +65.8%) are both independently corroborated via screener and CARE Ratings, AND fresh evidence (record order book, raised mid-year guidance) adds real commercial substance beyond the fundamentals alone.

Kept from High: rising debt (Rs579cr->Rs931cr) with high flagged borrowing cost, thin FCF conversion, a fresh single-month promoter stake reduction (66.50%->61.48%, likely a block deal given the simultaneous FII increase but not fully confirmed as such), and continued absence of any trusted/forum corroboration (246-post VP thread still not deep-read given its size) argue against going higher than Medium-High.

No red flag found - clean pledge declaration, no auditor resignation, no SEBI action. The promoter stake reduction was evaluated against the HIGH CAUTION 'promoter-holding collapse' criterion and judged not to meet that bar (promoter retains a clear majority at 61%, and the move coincides with an FII increase suggestive of an OFS/block deal rather than distress selling) - but it is flagged prominently for the next revisit.

four_box.note: Named T&D capex-cycle and export tailwind now backed by a record Rs9,217cr order book and raised guidance support tailwind/tam; moat stays weak (multiple large competitors adding capacity into the same cycle) and valuation stays weak (26.7x P/E against rising debt and thin FCF conversion, not clearly under-pricing the thesis). Score permits but does not require a 10x/100x label; kept 'neither' given capital-intensity/leverage (Nesco logic).

value_chain.theme: India T&D grid capex cycle + global transmission-tower/monopole export demand
value_chain.position: India's largest domestic manufacturer of transmission-line towers/structures, backward-integrated (own galvanizing/fabrication), diversifying into telecom towers and polymer pipes
value_chain.bottleneck_node: Engineering/tower manufacturing capacity (375,000 MTPA installed, targeting 600,000 MTPA by FY29 via ~Rs 500cr further capex)
value_chain.note: Multiple large T&D EPC/tower players (KEC, Kalpataru) are also expanding capacity alongside the PGCIL/state-transmission capex cycle - supply side is adding, not consolidating, so pricing power stays a function of capacity utilisation and order mix rather than a structural moat.

drivers: Operating leverage on a growing revenue base
Mix shift toward high-voltage (765kV) and export tower/monopole orders
earnings_quality.normalised_note: Current ~10.1% EBITDA margin (Q1 FY27) is below management's own stated long-term aspirational level of ~12% - not a spike, still building toward the stated target on mix/scale.

growth_trajectory.last_quarters_note: Annual YoY revenue growth: FY23 +16.0%, FY24 +65.8%, FY25 +40.9%, FY26 (actual) +20.1%, FY27 (management guidance) +15% - a clear, high-base deceleration, though still respectable double-digit growth each year.
growth_trajectory.reverse_pe_note: ~26.7x trailing P/E is not demanding against a ~60% 5-yr profit CAGR and management's own +30% FY27 PAT guidance, but the multiple assumes growth doesn't decelerate materially faster than the already-declining trend (65.8%->40.9%->20%->15% guided).

management_quality.capital_allocation: Reinvesting FY24-26 aggregate capex of ~Rs 867cr into capacity (300,000 -> 375,000 MTPA, targeting 600,000 by FY29), funded via internal accruals + term loan; incremental ROCE has risen alongside the capex cycle (9% -> 24%). No unrelated diversification found.
management_quality.capability_ladder_note: Explicit move up the value chain: from standard lattice-tower EPC toward 765kV high-voltage lines, monopoles, and a North America/LATAM export programme - management frames this as a deliberate mix-upgrade.

quality_metrics.note: Reconciles the original write-up's flagged 'unverified, possibly inflated' ROCE (~47.8%) and growth (~65.7%) figures using screener.in's FY-labelled tables: the real ROCE trend is 9-12% (FY20-22) improving to a genuine 21-24% (FY23-26) - strong but not the ~48% cited; the ~65.7% growth figure is CONFIRMED, not an artifact (FY24 was actually +65.8%). OPM has been remarkably stable (~9-10%) across 8 fiscal years, now edging toward management's ~12% aspirational target. FCF conversion is thin (~1% of EBITDA, FY26) as capex absorbs most operating cash flow. Gross borrowings have risen from ~Rs579cr (FY24) to ~Rs931cr (FY26) with cost of borrowing flagged high by screener, though CARE Ratings (A+/A1+, stable, Jun-2026) judges scheduled term-debt repayment comfortably covered by cash accruals. Separately: promoter holding fell 66.50% (Jun-26) -> 61.48% (Jul-26), a fresh ~5pp reduction concurrent with a sharp FII increase (4.11%->10.64%), consistent with a block deal rather than open-market selling but not fully confirmed as such this pass.

track_record.note: FY23 (+16.0% growth, ROCE 21%), FY24 (+65.8%, ROCE 24%), FY25 (+40.9%, ROCE 24%) and FY26 (+20.1%, ROCE 23.5%) each cleared BOTH >=10% revenue growth AND >=15% ROCE; FY20-22 did not clear (ROCE only 9-12% in that window). A genuine, now 4-year-running step-up in consistency, extended this pass with confirmed FY26 actuals.

shareholding_pattern.note: Promoter holding fell sharply from 66.50% (Jun-26) to 61.48% (Jul-26); FII holding rose sharply in the same window (4.11%->10.64%), consistent with a block deal/OFS moving shares to institutions rather than open-market distress selling. No pledge in either period, so concurrent_red_flag does not trigger (pledge is stable/zero, not rising). Worth confirming this isn't a sustained multi-quarter exit trend at the next revisit.

working_capital.note: CARE Ratings' own operating-cycle calculation shows genuine improvement (60 days FY25 -> 46 days FY26); this conflicts with screener.in's debtor-days metric (79->98 days), likely a different day-count methodology - not reconciled this pass. Net read: stable-to-improving working capital for an inherently capital-intensive, tender-based EPC/manufacturing business with 1-2 year execution cycles.
